correctness.rationale: Every forced adjacent chord is noncrossing and deletes without changing the crossing count; binomial expansion gives the polynomial identity. Exact coefficient comparison proves all mixed factorial moments. Uniform deletion of a random chord yields a crossing-monotone coupling. The crossing mean and variance are exact published identities. The factorial coefficients are bounded by 1 and tend to 1, enabling dominated convergence with the published crossing CLT to the independent Poisson–Gaussian product transform. A separate executed standard-library verifier passed 2945 exact integer/rational checks; no finite check is presented as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Microscopic adjacent pairings and macroscopic crossing complexity are canonical complementary statistics of perfect matchings. The exact identity controls arbitrary mixed factorial moments, establishes a universal nonpositive dependence with any increasing crossing test, and proves independence of nontrivial jointly scaled Poisson and Gaussian limits. This resolves a motivated joint-dependence gap left by published marginal analyses and is not just a one-parameter recalculation.
